entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Flavius Rusticius Helpidius was a prominent poet of the late Roman Empire.

Born around 500 CE in Rome, Italy, he rose to prominence during the reign of Emperor Justinian I (527–565 CE), who patronized the arts and literature.

Helpidius' most notable work is his poem 'De Morte et Reveniente', which explores themes of mortality, resurrection, and the afterlife.

His poetry reflects the spiritual concerns of Late Antiquity, particularly the Christian era, where he expressed a unique blend of paganism and Christian beliefs.

Flavius Rusticius Helpidius' legacy extends to the medieval period, where his works influenced the development of Latin literature in the Carolingian Renaissance.

He left behind a rich body of poetry that continues to be studied by scholars today for its historical insights into the late Roman Empire and the early Christian era.

With over 200 surviving lines of verse, Flavius Rusticius Helpidius remains one of the most celebrated poets of Late Antiquity, providing an unparalleled window into the spiritual, cultural, and artistic life of his time.
